title: Cam-Cleat Guy-Line Tensioner (3 parts)
description: Self-gripping cam cleat for tent and tarp lines: pull the cord and the spiral cam locks it; lift the tab to slide freely. Base, cam and pin.
use: Adjusts tent, tarp or clothesline tension without knots. Takes 2.5-4 mm cord. Screw or lash the base to a peg, tree strap or pole.
material: PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 5 perimeters, 100% infill on the cam. Teeth are printed; add a rubber band wrap for slick cord.
mechanism_tests: PASS | cam pose 0: vs base/cheeks: overlap 0.000 mm3 (must be 0)
PASS | cam pose 10: vs base/cheeks: overlap 0.000 mm3 (must be 0)
PASS | cam pose 20: vs base/cheeks: overlap 0.000 mm3 (must be 0)
PASS | cam pose 30: vs base/cheeks: overlap 0.000 mm3 (must be 0)
PASS | cam pose 45: vs base/cheeks: overlap 0.000 mm3 (must be 0)
PASS | cam pose 60: vs base/cheeks: overlap 0.000 mm3 (must be 0)
PASS | open pose 0 deg: cam clears cord by >= 0.4 mm (cord inflated 0.4): overlap 0.000 mm3 (must be 0)
PASS | open pose 10 deg: cam clears cord by >= 0.4 mm (cord inflated 0.4): overlap 0.000 mm3 (must be 0)
PASS | grip pose 40 deg: cam squeezes cord by 9.1 mm3 (>0 = grips)
PASS | grip pose 50 deg: cam squeezes cord by 22.0 mm3 (>0 = grips)
PASS | lever tab swings 40 deg from open to grip
problem_solved: Tent guy-lines normally need a knot (taut-line hitch) that is fiddly with cold hands or in the dark; metal cord locks are cheap but jam or rust. This gives a printable, self-tightening, tool-free line adjuster.
mechanism: Spiral cam on a 4 mm pin between two cheeks. The cam radius grows with rotation (8.6 to 14.6 mm), so pulling the cord rotates the cam into the cord; lifting the tab rotates it away.
tolerances: Cam 12 mm wide in 13 mm cheek gap (0.5 mm each side); pin 2.0 mm radius in cheek holes 2.1 (press) and cam bore 2.4 (free); open-pose gap to a 3.4 mm cord >= 0.4 mm; grip squeeze starts near 30-40 deg.
assembly: 2. Lay the cam between the cheeks and push the pin through both cheeks and the cam.
3. Thread cord under the cam along the base channel.
fit_notes: Cord friction varies a lot - slick Dyneema may slip. Grip not yet measured.
